qa_pairs.question: How can users access the Nibi cluster?
qa_pairs.answer: Users can access the Nibi cluster through Open OnDemand (OOD), a web-based platform available at https://ondemand.sharcnet.ca/. After signing in with multifactor authentication, they can open a Bash shell terminal or launch a remote desktop session via the user-friendly web interface.

qa_pairs.question: What is the `/scratch` storage quota policy for users on the Nibi cluster?
qa_pairs.answer: Each user on the Nibi cluster has a 1 TB soft quota for `/scratch` storage. This soft quota can be exceeded for up to 60 days, after which no additional files may be written or expanded until the user's total `/scratch` usage drops below 1 TB.

qa_pairs.question: How do I request specific Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) H100 instances for a compute job on the Nibi cluster?
qa_pairs.answer: To request a single MIG H100 GPU instance for a compute job on Nibi, use the appropriate Slurm option: for an H100-1g.10gb instance with 10GB memory, use `--gpus=h100_1g.10gb:1`; for an H100-2g.20gb instance with 20GB, use `--gpus=h100_2g.20gb:1`; and for an H100-3g.40gb instance with 40GB, use `--gpus=h100_3g.40gb:1`.
